**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

Section 6.3 of the Transfer and Servicing Agreement gives us a genuine counterparty indemnity running in our favour:

- **Scope/direction:** Cellco as Servicer (6.3(a)(i)) and separately as Marketing Agent (6.3(a)(ii)) indemnifies the Issuer, Owner Trustee and Indenture Trustee and their officers, directors, employees and agents for all fees, expenses, losses, claims, damages and liabilities, including reasonable legal fees and the cost of enforcing the indemnity, resulting from its willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence.
- **Procedure:** 6.3(b) has the usual mechanics — prompt notice that is not a strict condition absent prejudice, counterparty defence with counsel reasonably satisfactory to us, separate counsel at its cost on conflict, and no settlement implying our acknowledgement of a claim without consent.
- **No cap, no reciprocity problem:** the indemnity is uncapped, survives resignation/termination (6.3(c)), and there is no Issuer/Depositor indemnity of the Servicer anywhere in the document. Section 7.5(c) also puts transition expenses on the outgoing Servicer.

Noted but not flagged: no IP-infringement trigger (atypical for a receivables securitisation with no licensed services or deliverables), no standalone breach-of-law or data-breach trigger (Exhibit A privacy/data-protection policies and the 6.2(a) liability standard partly cover this), and the Depositor is not named as an Indemnified Person. These are sub-elements short of the preferred wording rather than material failures of the fallback, so we leave the clause as drafted.
